dedication.text: To my beautiful wife, Sharon, who walked arm in arm with me through a Total Money Makeover—I love you, honey. To the superstars all across America who have had the courage to face the person in the mirror, the culture, their family, and even their coworkers as they 'lived like no one else so later they could live like no one else.' You who have courageously had a Total Money Makeover of the heart and wallet are the real superstars. To the Dave Ramsey team and the Thomas Nelson team for tireless hours on this project to make this material available to everyone across this great land.

introduction.title: Introduction
introduction.core_philosophy: Personal finance is 80 percent behavior and only 20 percent head knowledge.
key_statements: The problem with my money is the guy in my mirror. If he will behave, he can make the money thing work.
The math of wealth building is not rocket science; it is simple—but you have to DO IT!
This proven plan is having a national impact because I have realized that to change your money thing, you have to change.
The principles are not mine. I stole them all from God and your grandmother.
I am positive that personal finance is 80 percent behavior and only 20 percent head knowledge.

author_background.financial_peace_university: Thirteen-week class with over 1 million families attending
author_background.personal_experience: Went broke, rebuilt wealth twice; first time in real estate, second time debt-free

introduction.promise_to_reader: If you will follow the guidelines of this proven system of sacrifice and discipline, you can be debt-free, begin saving, and give as you've never given before. You will build wealth.

sections.heading: This Book Is NOT Sophisticated or Complicated
sections.content: Not a detailed, in-depth guide to investing. The most profound and life-changing truths are very simple. Millionaires keep their investing and money philosophies very uncomplicated.

sections.heading: This Book Is NOT Something That Has Never Been Said
sections.content: Very little in this book is something that someone else has not written or said. The author has packaged time-honored information into a process that is doable and has inspired millions to act.

sections.heading: This Book Is NOT Going to Mislead You on Investment Returns
sections.content: Recommends good growth stock-type mutual funds as long-term investment with 12% return. The S&P 500 has averaged 11.67% per year for the last 80+ years. This includes the big drop in the 2008 market.

sections.heading: This Book Is NOT Written by Someone with No Academic Credentials
sections.content: Author has a degree in finance and is licensed in real estate, insurance, and investments. The biggest qualifier is personal experience: went broke and rebuilt wealth twice. 'Don't take financial advice from broke people.'

sections.heading: This Book Is NOT Politically Correct
sections.content: Openly discusses the spiritual aspects of money and behavior. Includes Bible verses as a Christian author. Behavior intelligently viewed takes into account emotional, relational, family history, socioeconomic impacts, and the spiritual.

sections.heading: This Book Is NOT Wrong
sections.content: Extreme confidence based on millions of people who have benefited. The principles are responsible for changing lives. The same questions always get the same answers because the principles stand and work every time.

sections.heading: This Book Is NOT the Same As My Other Books
sections.content: Financial Peace is 'what to do with money.' The Total Money Makeover is more than a 'what to do' book—it is a 'how to do it' plan. A process-driven work weaving inspiration and information into a step-by-step plan.

sections.heading: This Book Is NOT Getting Any Complaints or Criticism
sections.content: ...from people who do it. No one who has gotten on a budget, gotten out of debt, gotten on the same page with their spouse, and built wealth has said they HATE IT.

flying_turkeys_and_skinny_dipping.title: Flying Turkeys and Skinny Dipping
flying_turkeys_and_skinny_dipping.three_little_pigs_lesson: Those who build on solid foundations survive economic storms. Those who build 'quick and dirty' find their lives blown apart.

2008_economic_crisis_analysis.cause: Broke people in serious financial trouble borrowed money from greedy bankers at horrible terms and high interest rates to buy homes. SUBprime loans were packaged together and sold as bonds.
2008_economic_crisis_analysis.effect: Foreclosure numbers rose, home prices dropped, fear broke out on Wall Street, stock prices dropped, consumer spending stopped, businesses died, unemployment rose.
2008_economic_crisis_analysis.lesson: Your financial process and principles must work in good times and in bad times—otherwise, they don't work.
2008_economic_crisis_analysis.flying_turkey_metaphor: Even a turkey can fly in a tornado. When times are booming, you can do dumb things with money and seem to get away with it. When the storm hits, stupid comes up looking stupid.
2008_economic_crisis_analysis.skinny_dipping_metaphor: When the tide goes out, you can tell who was skinny-dipping. The 2008 crisis revealed who had built on solid financial foundations.

flying_turkeys_and_skinny_dipping.key_quote: People were running around, buying things they couldn't afford with money they didn't have, to impress people they didn't even like.

chapters.title: The Total Money Makeover Challenge
chapters.core_message: The challenge is YOU. You are the problem with your money, and you are the solution.

key_concepts.explanation: The financial channel or some DVD sets aren't your answer; you are. You are the king of your future. The Total Money Makeover plan works because it is simple and gets to the heart of your money problems: you.

IF YOU WILL LIVE LIKE NO ONE ELSE, LATER YOU CAN LIVE LIKE NO ONE ELSE. If you will make the sacrifices now that most people aren't willing to make, later on you will be able to live as those folks will never be able to live.
Most folks have a good idea of what to do with money but not how to do it. The problem with money is the guy in the mirror. If he will behave, he can make the money thing work.
If you will follow the guidelines of this proven system of sacrifice and discipline, you can be debt-free, begin saving, and give as you've never given before. It is totally up to you.

shocking_stats: 90% of people in our culture buy things they can't afford.

success_stories.debt_paid: $57,000 in six months (plus $7,000 given to church)
success_stories.key_lesson: The key to success was both of us getting on the same page at the same time. We now work together to plan our spending rather than racing to outspend each other.

dave_rants: Savings without a mission is garbage. Your money needs to work for you, not lie around.

chapters.title: Denial: I'm Not That Out of Shape
chapters.core_message: Ninety percent of solving a problem is realizing there is one. Denial is one of the four major factors that keep people from winning with money.

key_concepts.explanation: When you are physically fat, it is hard to be in denial, because there is the ever-widening belt line. When you are financially fat, you can fake it and look good for a while. Friends and family participate in your fantasy/denial.

If you put a frog in boiling water, it will jump out. But if you put it in cool water and slowly raise the temperature, it will stay until it dies. Many people slowly accumulate debt without realizing the danger.
Look in the mirror. Take a long look. Being financially mediocre in this country is pretty much okay by most folks' standards. But this is a book about winning, about really having something.

myths_vs_truth.myth: Debt consolidation saves interest, and you have one smaller payment.
myths_vs_truth.truth: Debt consolidation is dangerous because you treat only the symptom.

success_stories.debt_paid: $16,000 in consumer debt in ten months
success_stories.key_lesson: Dave helped us realize that we had to draw the line and stop living beyond our means.

case_studies.name: Sara and John
case_studies.situation: Combined income $75,000, small student loan, car loan, $5,000 credit card, new home. Sara lost her $45,000 job in September.
case_studies.lesson: If life isn't smacking you around at the moment, you are actually in greater danger. You are a real candidate for financial mediocrity or even a major crisis brought on by denial.

dave_rants: For your own good, for the good of your family and your future, grow a backbone. When something is wrong, stand up and say it is wrong, and don't back down.

chapters.title: Debt Myths: Debt Is (Not) a Tool
chapters.core_message: Debt is not a tool; it is a method to make banks wealthy, not you. The borrower is slave to the lender.

myths_vs_truth.myth: Debt is a tool and should be used to create prosperity.
myths_vs_truth.truth: Debt is not a tool; it is a method to make banks wealthy, not you. The borrower is slave to the lender (Proverbs 22:7).

myths_vs_truth.myth: If I loan money to a friend or relative, I will help them out.
myths_vs_truth.truth: If you loan money to a friend or relative, you will likely damage or destroy the relationship.

myths_vs_truth.myth: By cosigning a loan, I am helping out a friend or relative.
myths_vs_truth.truth: Cosigning is stupid. According to Proverbs 17:18, 'It's stupid to guarantee someone else's loan.'

myths_vs_truth.myth: Cash Advance, Payday Loans, Rent-to-Own, Title Pawning, and Tote-the-Note Car Lots are needed to help lower-income people get ahead.
myths_vs_truth.truth: These rip-off examples of predatory lending are designed to take advantage of lower-income people and benefit only the owners of the companies making the loans.

myths_vs_truth.myth: 'Ninety days same as cash' equals using other people's money for free.
myths_vs_truth.truth: Ninety days is not the same as cash. 88% of these contracts convert to debt at 24-38% interest, back-charged to date of purchase.

myths_vs_truth.myth: Car payments are a way of life; you'll always have one.
myths_vs_truth.truth: Staying away from car payments by driving reliable used cars is what the average millionaire does; that is how he or she became a millionaire.

myths_vs_truth.myth: Leasing a car is what sophisticated financial people do.
myths_vs_truth.truth: Leasing a car is the most expensive way to operate a vehicle. The average car lease payment is $495 per month. A car lease is 'fleecing.'

key_statistics: The Federal Reserve notes that the average car payment is $495 over sixty-four months.
If you invested $495 per month from age 25 to age 65 at 12% average, you would have $5,881,799.14 at age 65.
Payday loan interest rates are over 650% annually.
Rent-to-Own effective interest rates are over 1,800% on average (Federal Trade Commission).
88% of '90 days same as cash' contracts convert to debt.
Over 97% of people don't systematically pay extra on their mortgage.

predatory_lending_types.description: Write a hot check for $225, dated one week from now (payday). They give you $200 cash. The $25 service charge equates to over 650% interest annually.
Dealer purchases cheap cars and sells them with down payment equal to what he paid. Payments at 18-38% interest paid weekly. Cars repeatedly repo'd and resold.
predatory_lending_types.verdict: The down payment could have purchased the car if the buyer had been more savvy.

predatory_lending_types.description: Effective interest rates over 1,800% on average. A washer/dryer costs $20/week for 90 weeks = $1,800 total, vs. $500 new retail or $200 used.
predatory_lending_types.verdict: The worst example of 'I want it now' mentality.

car_payment_math.lifetime_cost_of_car_payments: $5,881,799.14 if invested at 12% from age 25 to 65
car_payment_math.alternative: Save $495/month for 10 months = $5,000 cash car; trade up every 10 months
car_payment_math.recommendation: Drive reliable used cars. The average millionaire drives a used car.

success_stories.key_lesson: We now talk about our finances instead of just fighting about money. My wife and I have been debt-free since January of 2004, and life is so much easier now.

chapters.title: Money Myths: The (Non) Secrets of the Rich
chapters.core_message: There are no secrets to wealth. Get-rich-quick schemes don't work. The lottery is a tax on the poor. Real wealth is built through hard work, living on less than you make, and investing.

myths_vs_truth.myth: You can get rich quick if you just know the right secrets.
myths_vs_truth.truth: No one gets rich quick by using secret information. Energy, thrift, and diligence are how wealth is built, not dumb luck.

myths_vs_truth.myth: Cash Value life insurance, like Whole Life, will help me retire wealthy.
myths_vs_truth.truth: Cash Value life insurance is one of the worst financial products available. Over 70% of life insurance policies sold today are Cash Value policies.

details.recommendation: Buy 20-year level term insurance and invest the difference in mutual funds.

myths_vs_truth.myth: Playing the lottery and other forms of gambling will make you rich.
myths_vs_truth.truth: The lottery is a tax on the poor and on people who can't do math. Zip codes that spend four times what anyone else does on lottery tickets are in lower-income parts of town.

myths_vs_truth.myth: Mobile homes (trailers) will allow me to own something instead of renting, and that will help me become wealthy.
myths_vs_truth.truth: Trailers go down in value rapidly. A $25,000 double-wide home will be worth $8,000 in five years while you still owe $22,000.

myths_vs_truth.myth: Prepaying my funeral or my kids' college expenses is a good way to invest and protect myself against inflation.
myths_vs_truth.truth: Plans for prepaid funerals and college expenses give low rates of return and put money in the other guy's pocket. Prepaying tuition = 8% return; mutual funds = 12% return.

myths_vs_truth.myth: I don't have time to work on a budget, retirement plan, or estate plan.
myths_vs_truth.truth: You don't have time not to. A budget is people telling their money where to go instead of wondering where it went (John Maxwell).

myths_vs_truth.myth: The debt-management companies on TV, like AmeriDebt, will save me.
myths_vs_truth.truth: You may get out of debt, but only with your credit trashed. Using debt management companies is treated the same as filing Chapter 13 Bankruptcy for mortgage underwriting.

cash_value_policy.death_benefit: Face value only ($125,000); savings do NOT go to family

term_insurance_alternative.remaining_$93: Should be invested in mutual funds
term_insurance_alternative.advantage: When 20-year term expires, if you've invested well, you are self-insured

dave_rants: Whole Life insurance is a horrible product. Why would you pay someone interest on your own savings? That's backward, and it does not make you smart.

chapters.title: Two More Hurdles: Ignorance and Keeping Up with the Joneses
chapters.core_message: Two final obstacles before climbing the mountain: financial ignorance and peer pressure (keeping up with the Joneses). The Joneses are broke.

key_concepts.explanation: Ignorance is not lack of intelligence; it is simply 'not knowing.' Many intelligent but ignorant people make terrible financial decisions. The cure for ignorance is education and action.
We buy things we don't need with money we don't have in order to impress people we don't like. The Joneses are broke. Quit trying to keep up with them.

Everyone has a weak spot—something they spend money on to impress others. Until you recognize that weak area, you will always be prone to financial stupidity on that subject. The author's weak spot was cars (Jaguar).

Author went broke while keeping his Jaguar, even having his electricity cut off while the Jaguar sat in the driveway. Eventually sold the Jaguar on a Thursday because the bank would repo it on Friday. Lesson: Don't let image drive financial decisions.

key_quotes: We buy things we don't need with money we don't have in order to impress people we don't like.
Looking good is when your broke friends are impressed by what you drive, and being good is having more money than they have.

success_stories.key_lesson: My wife and I have been debt-free since January of 2004, and life is so much easier now.

chapters.transition: Past the Obstacle Course and Up the Mountain: Having overcome denial, debt myths, money myths, ignorance, and peer pressure, you are now ready to climb the mountain using the Baby Steps.

chapters.title: Save $1,000 Fast: Walk Before You Run
chapters.subtitle: Baby Step 1
chapters.baby_step_title: Save $1,000 in a Starter Emergency Fund
chapters.core_message: The Baby Steps work because of the power of focus and the power of priority. Do one step at a time, in order.

baby_steps_overview.title: Save $1,000 Fast (Starter Emergency Fund)
baby_steps_overview.description: Walk before you run. Build a small emergency fund to prevent new debt when unexpected expenses arise.

baby_steps_overview.title: The Debt Snowball
baby_steps_overview.description: Pay off all debt (except the house) using the Debt Snowball method.

baby_steps_overview.title: Invest 15% of Income in Retirement
baby_steps_overview.description: Invest 15% of household income into Roth IRAs and pre-tax retirement plans.

baby_steps_overview.title: College Funding
baby_steps_overview.description: Save for children's college using ESAs and 529 plans.

why_baby_steps_work: Power of Focus: When you try to do everything at once, progress is very slow. Focused intensity causes things to happen.
Power of Priority: Each step builds on the one before. Done out of order, they do not work.
Quick Wins: Paying off small debts first fires you up and keeps you motivated.
Behavior Modification: The steps address behavior change, not just math.

key_concepts.explanation: The way you eat an elephant is one bite at a time. Find something to do and do that with vigor until it is complete; then and only then do you move to the next step.
A 350-pound person beginning marathon training with a quick ten-mile run would have a heart attack. Build up gradually. The $1,000 emergency fund is your base camp.

shocking_stats: 90% of airline miles 'rewarded' are never redeemed.

chapters.title: The Debt Snowball: Lose Weight Fast, Really
chapters.subtitle: Baby Step 2
chapters.baby_step_title: Pay Off All Debt (Except the House) Using the Debt Snowball
chapters.core_message: List debts smallest to largest. Pay minimum payments on all except the smallest. Attack the smallest with every dollar you can find. When it's paid off, roll that payment to the next. Gazelle intensity required.

debt_snowball_method.step_1: List all debts from smallest to largest by total payoff amount (not interest rate).
debt_snowball_method.step_2: Pay minimum payments on all debts except the smallest.
debt_snowball_method.step_3: Attack the smallest debt with every extra dollar you can find.
debt_snowball_method.step_4: When the smallest is paid off, take that payment and add it to the minimum payment on the next smallest debt.
debt_snowball_method.step_5: Repeat until all debts (except the house) are paid off.
debt_snowball_method.key_rule: Do NOT list by interest rate. List by balance. The quick wins are more important than the math.
debt_snowball_method.why_smallest_first: Behavior modification over math. Quick wins keep you motivated. If you go on a diet and lose weight the first week, you will stay on that diet.

gazelle_intensity.definition: Total, sold-out, focused intensity. To the exclusion of virtually everything else, getting out of debt.
gazelle_intensity.biblical_reference: Proverbs 6:1 and 5: 'Deliver yourself like the bird from the hand of the fowler and the gazelle from the hand of the hunter.'
gazelle_intensity.cheetah_vs_gazelle: The cheetah (fastest mammal) only catches its prey 1 in 19 chases because the gazelle outmaneuvers it. The way out of debt is to outmaneuver the enemy and run for your life.
gazelle_intensity.practical_application: Stop all non-essential spending. Cut up credit cards NOW. Sell things. Take extra jobs. Attack debt with everything you have.

how_to_get_snowball_rolling: Use the Pro Rata plan if you can't make minimum payments
Stop borrowing immediately—draw a line in the sand
key_quotes: To the exclusion of virtually everything else, I'm getting out of debt!
The way out of debt is to outmaneuver the enemy and run for your life.
You can't get out of a hole by digging out the bottom.

success_stories.debt_paid: $95,000+ in student loans, cars, and credit cards in 35 months
success_stories.key_lesson: We literally changed our family tree—all because we bothered and cared enough to do something about it.

success_stories.debt_paid: $169,000+ in 6 months (sold rental property, BMW, everything)
success_stories.key_lesson: The most important part of this whole process was learning to delay pleasure.
The ability to become debt-free isn't contingent upon a certain income. It is all about changing behavior and being intense about getting rid of that nasty debt!

chapters.title: Finish the Emergency Fund: Kick Murphy Out
chapters.subtitle: Baby Step 3
chapters.baby_step_title: Save 3-6 Months of Expenses in a Fully Funded Emergency Fund
chapters.core_message: Murphy's Law: Whatever can go wrong will go wrong. An emergency fund is insurance against life's unexpected events. It transforms emergencies into mere inconveniences.

emergency_fund_details.where_to_keep: Money Market account with check-writing privileges
emergency_fund_details.purpose: Not for investments, not for planned purchases—only for true emergencies
what_does_not_count: Christmas (not an emergency—it comes every year)

murphy_metaphor.description: Murphy's Law says if something can go wrong, it will. Murphy visits everyone. The emergency fund kicks Murphy out of your house.
murphy_metaphor.transformation: What used to be a huge, life-altering event will become a mere inconvenience when you have an emergency fund.

clarifications.situation: Twins due in 6 months / Plant closing in 4 months / Received $25,000 severance
clarifications.action: Temporarily stop the Debt Snowball and concentrate on the emergency fund because storm clouds are visible and real.
Still need an emergency fund. Even if income is guaranteed, you might need to help a sick relative, replace your heating system, or get a new transmission.
Save for down payment or cash purchase after completing Baby Steps 2 and 3. This is Baby Step 3(b). Do NOT buy a home while still broke.

chapters.timeline: Getting to the end of this step if you are gazelle-intense takes the typical family 24 to 30 months from starting the Total Money Makeover.
chapters.result: Debt-free except for the house, with 3-6 months of expenses saved (approximately $10,000+). No payments except the house payment.

success_stories.situation: Single mom of two, started business at 23, reached $100,000 in debt
success_stories.result: Debt-free except house, $2M term life insurance, $3,000/month savings for education, emergency fund, and investments
success_stories.key_lesson: Goal is to be completely debt-free, including the house, by age 35.

chapters.title: Maximize Retirement Investing: Be Financially Healthy for Life
chapters.subtitle: Baby Step 4
chapters.baby_step_title: Invest 15% of Household Income into Roth IRAs and Pre-Tax Retirement Plans
chapters.core_message: Invest 15% of before-tax gross income annually toward retirement. The magic of compound interest works for you. Start now—you can't get that time back.

the_15_percent_rule.why_not_more: You need some income left for college saving (Step 5) and paying off the home (Step 6).
the_15_percent_rule.why_not_less: Kids' college degrees won't feed you at retirement. You need retirement investing before college saving and mortgage payoff.

stats: More than 70% of Americans do not believe they will be able to retire with dignity (Bankrate.com).
40% of people making less than $35,000/year say the best way to have $500,000 at retirement is to win the Lotto (Consumer Federation of America).
80% of Americans believe their standard of living will go up at retirement (Wealth Builder magazine).
Out of 100 people age 65: 97 can't write a check for $600, 54 are still working, only 3 are financially secure (USA Today).
Bankruptcies among those 65 and older went up 244% in a ten-year period.

investment_order.reason: The employer match is a 100% return on investment—always take the free money first.
Grows tax-FREE. Best long-term investment vehicle available.
Pre-tax growth. Complete the 15% with pre-tax contributions.

mutual_fund_types.description: Large-cap stocks. More stable. Lower growth.
Small-cap stocks. Higher risk, higher potential return.

what_retirement_means.traditional_view: Save enough money so I can quit the job I hate.
what_retirement_means.ramsey_view: Security means choices. Work is an option. You can choose to write a book, design churches, or spend time with grandkids.
what_retirement_means.harold_fisher_example: 100 years old, worked five days a week at the architectural firm he founded. 'People who retire early, die early.'

key_quotes: Simple maintenance will keep your money muscles maintained.
If you hate your career path, change it.
This is not the time to give yourself a raise!

success_stories.occupations: Technical specialist for natural gas pipeline (retired); Nurse and stay-at-home mom (retired)
success_stories.result: Retired at age 58 (7 years early) with approximately $1,000,000 in retirement accounts on never more than $60,000/year income
success_stories.key_lesson: Always put 10% of check into stock purchase plan. At first didn't think could afford it, but figured in the long run couldn't afford not to.

chapters.title: College Funding: Make Sure the Kids Are Fit Too
chapters.subtitle: Baby Step 5
chapters.baby_step_title: Save for Children's College Using ESAs and 529 Plans
chapters.core_message: Save for college tax-free using Educational Savings Accounts (ESAs) and 529 plans. Avoid student loans. College is possible without debt through creativity and resourcefulness.

stats: Only 9% of families use college savings funds like ESAs and 529 plans (2008 SallieMae/Gallup study).
91% have saved nothing or close to nothing toward college.
College tuition inflation averages about 8% per year vs. 4% general inflation.
37% of the few who save for college do so in a simple savings account yielding less than 3%.

savings_vehicles.tax_treatment: Grows tax-FREE when used for higher education
savings_vehicles.flexibility: Can invest anywhere, in any fund or mix of funds, change at will
savings_vehicles.recommendation: First choice. Most flexible, most control.
savings_vehicles.example: $166.67/month ($2,000/year) from birth to age 18 at 12% = $126,000 tax-free

types_to_avoid: Life phase plans (8% return, very conservative)
Fixed portfolio plans (locked in, can't move money)
savings_vehicles.recommended_type: Flexible plan allowing movement within a family of funds
savings_vehicles.advantage: Can save in any state's plan and use at any institution of higher learning
savings_vehicles.recommendation: Second choice after ESA. Only use the flexible type.

savings_vehicles.verdict: Not recommended. You simply break even with tuition inflation.
A joke. Do not use for college savings.
Won't work for college savings. Below tuition inflation rate.

monthly_college_planning_factors.description: To determine monthly savings needed at 12% interest (8% net after 4% inflation)
monthly_college_planning_factors.example: Multiply annual college cost (today's dollars) by factor to get monthly savings needed

creative_college_funding_strategies: Start at community college (much cheaper) then transfer to 4-year school
Apply for scholarships (hundreds of millions available annually, not just academic/athletic)
Work-study programs (e.g., UPS pays tuition for 20 hours/week work)
Military service (4 years = free college education)
National Guard (boot camp + tuition and books)
Underserved areas programs (government pays for school or pays off student loans)
Live at home, eat cafeteria food, drive 20 miles each way if needed
chapters.student_loans_stance: Student loans are off-limits. A legacy of debt should not be passed down your family tree.

success_stories.result: Daughter graduated with no student loans using community college, scholarships, and teamwork
success_stories.key_lesson: With a little creativity and a lot of hard work, we really could pay cash for our daughter's education.

success_stories.result: Paid off cars and $36,000 in student loans before marriage, saved $9,000 for wedding
success_stories.key_lesson: It's a great feeling to be planning for what's ahead of you instead of having to pay off your past.

success_stories.result: Paid off $35,000 in debt on $35,000 income by working 2-3 jobs simultaneously
success_stories.key_lesson: Having a plan for my money changed my life!

chapters.title: Pay Off the Home Mortgage: Be Ultrafit
chapters.subtitle: Baby Step 6
chapters.core_message: Become completely debt-free. No payments. The grass feels different under your feet when you own it. Don't settle for 'The Good Enough' at the 18-mile mark of the marathon.

mortgage_myths_debunked.myth: It is wise to keep my home mortgage to get the tax deduction.
mortgage_myths_debunked.truth: Tax deductions are no bargain. If you pay $10,000 in interest to get a $3,000 tax deduction, you've lost $7,000. 'I will personally pay $3,000 of your taxes as soon as your check for $10,000 clears into my bank account.'

mortgage_myths_debunked.myth: It is wise to borrow all I can on my home (or continually refinance for cash out) because of the great interest rates; then I can invest the money.
mortgage_myths_debunked.truth: You really don't make anything when the smoke clears. After adjusting for taxes (30% bracket = $2,400-$3,600 tax on gains) and risk (debt increases risk), the debt-free person comes out ahead.
mortgage_myths_debunked.math: Borrow $100,000 at 8% = $8,000 interest. Invest at 12% = $12,000 return. Minus 30% taxes = $8,400-$9,600 net. Net gain: $400-$1,600. Not worth the risk.

mortgage_myths_debunked.myth: Take out a thirty-year mortgage and promise yourself to pay it like a fifteen-year, so if something goes wrong you have wiggle room.
mortgage_myths_debunked.truth: Something will go wrong. You don't have that kind of discipline. Put systems in place that make you do smart things. Get a 15-year fixed-rate mortgage.

mortgage_myths_debunked.myth: The home-equity loan is good to have instead of an emergency fund.
mortgage_myths_debunked.truth: Emergencies are precisely when you don't need debt. HELs (Home Equity Loans) are very dangerous. An unbelievable amount end in foreclosure.

mortgage_myths_debunked.myth: You can't pay cash for a home!
mortgage_myths_debunked.truth: Paying cash for a home is possible, very possible. What's hard to find is people willing to pay the price in sacrificed lifestyle.

mortgage_guidelines.maximum_payment: No more than 25% of take-home pay
mortgage_guidelines.recommendation: Never take more than a 15-year fixed-rate loan
mortgage_guidelines.100_percent_down_plan: Pay cash for a home. Luke and his wife saved $50,000/year for 3 years on $80,000 household income and paid cash for a $150,000 home at age 26.

mortgage_payment_table.example: Sale Price $150,000, 15 years at 6%: $150,000 / $1,000 = 150 × 8.44 = $1,266 monthly payment

refinancing_guide.formula: Current payment - New payment = Monthly savings. Closing costs / Monthly savings = Months to break even.
refinancing_guide.example: $1,434 current - $1,307 new = $127 savings. $2,300 closing costs / $127 = 18 months to break even.
refinancing_guide.rule: If you will stay in your home longer than the break-even period, you are a candidate for refinancing.

arm_guide.description: How to Figure the Change in Your Adjustable Rate Mortgage
arm_guide.warning: Almost all ARMs start below margin the first year, guaranteeing a payment increase at anniversary unless rates DROP.

chapters.timeline: Families who stay gazelle-intense pay off the mortgage about seven years from the date they declared war on the culture.

success_stories.result: Started with $3,000 home equity loan, credit card bills, $30,000 mortgage on $45,000 income. Paid off house in September 2005. Completely DEBT-FREE.
success_stories.key_lesson: It's unbelievable the feeling of freedom that comes when you don't have the weight of payments hanging over your head.

success_stories.result: Paid off house a year and a half ahead of schedule
success_stories.key_lesson: The peace we have from being debt-free is worth the small sacrifices.

success_stories.name: Alicia (Al)
success_stories.situation: Started Total Money Makeover at age 25 with $118,000 in total debt on $70,000 household income
success_stories.result: Paid off every red cent in six years. Debt-free at 31.
success_stories.key_lesson: The grass really does feel different under my bare feet in the backyard now that there is no mortgage and we are DEBT-FREE!

chapters.title: Build Wealth Like Crazy: Arnold Schwarzedollar, Mr. Universe of Money
chapters.subtitle: Baby Step 7
chapters.core_message: You have entered the top 2% of Americans. Totally debt-free. Now build wealth intentionally for three purposes: FUN, INVESTING, and GIVING.

three_uses_of_money.description: Money is good for fun. After all the sacrifice, enjoy the rewards. Buy the Harley, take the cruise, buy the diamond. The problem is people buy these things when they can't afford them.
three_uses_of_money.example: Michael: $550,000/year average income, $20 million in investments. 'Buy the Harley, dude!'

three_uses_of_money.description: Investing is how you keep on winning. It becomes like Monopoly—'a little bit like Monopoly.' Keep investing simple: mutual funds and debt-free real estate.
advice: Always manage your own money—surround yourself with advisors but you make the decisions.
Keep investing very simple until you have over $10 million.
Use simple mutual funds and debt-free real estate.
Ride out market fluctuations—stay in for the long term.
Never cash out at the bottom of the market.

three_uses_of_money.description: Giving is possibly the most fun you will ever have with money. The thing the healthy wealthy ones share in common is a love of GIVING.
examples: Friend buys 75 brand-new bikes for inner-city ministry every Christmas
Seeds of Kindness: $50,000 given away $100 at a time, human to human
Secret Santa (Larry Stewart): Gave away over $1.3 million in $100 bills on the streets
three_uses_of_money.monkey_trap_metaphor: Monkeys trapped by heavy glass bottles with nuts inside—can't remove fist without dropping nuts. Don't let greed trap you.

pinnacle_point.definition: The point at which your money works harder than you do. When your money makes more than you do, you are officially wealthy.
pinnacle_point.calculation: Multiply nest egg by 0.08 (8%). If you can live on that number, you have reached the Pinnacle Point.
pinnacle_point.description: Like reaching the top of a hill on a bike—the glorious ride down begins. Money takes on a life of its own. Wealth will find its way to you.
pinnacle_point.bike_hill_metaphor: The switchback technique: painfully going side to side, taking small bites at a time of the mountain. Then the perfect moment at the top before the glorious ride down.

wealth_team_criteria: Heart of a teacher, not a salesman or 'expert'
Can explain complex issues in ways you can understand
Will not just say 'because I say so'
Be aware of possible conflicts of interest (commission-based advisors)
key_quotes: Wealth is not an escape mechanism. It is instead a tremendous responsibility.
When your money makes more than you do, you are officially wealthy.
Money is a hard worker, harder than you. Money never gets sick, never gets pregnant, and is never disabled.

success_stories.result: Paid off $50,000 mortgage in less than 4 years on teacher's salary (under $40,000). Adopted two girls from China. Now give freely.
success_stories.key_lesson: We give like never before; we save like never before; and, most important, we live life the way God intended us to like never before.

success_stories.result: Paid off $50,000. Debt-free except house. Paid daughter's friend's private school tuition for a year.
success_stories.key_lesson: Buying things may feel good, but giving always feels right.

success_stories.result: Debt-free including house. $100,000 in retirement funds, $90,000 in savings, house worth $450,000, paid cash for two newer cars.
success_stories.key_lesson: My status symbol of choice is the paid-off home mortgage AND the BMW in the driveway.

chapters.title: Live Like No One Else
chapters.core_message: The Total Money Makeover is more than a discussion on money. It makes you face the man or woman in the mirror. The danger of wealth is becoming enamored with it. Wealth is a tool and a responsibility, not the answer to life's questions.

warnings_about_wealth.description: A malady affecting the affluent who seek happiness, solace, and fulfillment in the consuming of stuff. They come up empty and end up depressed. 'He who dies with the most toys is still dead.'
Proverbs 10:15: A rich man's wealth can become his walled city. If all you get from your wealth is the wrong view of it, wealth will destroy your peace.
Wealth will make you more of what you are. If you are a jerk and become wealthy, you will be king of the jerks. If you are generous and become wealthy, you will be most generous.

wealth_and_spirituality.misconception: Some political and religious groups have decided that wealth is evil.
wealth_and_spirituality.truth: Many heroes of biblical faith were very wealthy: King David, Solomon, Job, most Founding Fathers.
wealth_and_spirituality.dallas_willard_quote: To use riches is to cause them to be consumed, to trust in riches is to count upon them for things they cannot provide, but to possess riches is to have the right to say how they will or will not be used.
wealth_and_spirituality.ramsey_position: If you are a good person, it is your spiritual duty to possess riches for the good of mankind. Good people must get wealth to keep it from the bad people, because the good people will do good with it.

final_message.hope: Hope is what I want you to walk away with from this book. Hope that you can be like the people whose stories I told. Hope that you can retire with dignity. Hope that you can change your family tree. Hope that you can give money in a way you have never given before.
final_message.call_to_action: It is time for you to become a gazelle. It is time for you to leave the reading and the classroom behind and apply these principles. They are age-old principles, and they work.
final_message.encouragement: Tens of thousands of ordinary people just like you and me have become debt-free and even wealthy using this plan. It isn't magic; it is common sense. The exciting thing is, anyone can do this—anyone. Are you next?

key_quotes: The Total Money Makeover makes you face the man or woman in the mirror.
Wealth is not the answer to life's questions.
The LOVE of Money, Not Money, Is the Root of All Evil.
It is time for you to become a gazelle.

winners_section.title: Meet The Winners of The Total Money Makeover Challenge
winners_section.contest_description: When The Total Money Makeover first released, a contest was held to see who could have the greatest change in financial position in a six-month period. Hundreds entered. Ten finalists went to Atlantis (Bahamas). One family won the $50,000 grand prize.

actions_taken: Lived on written budget for first time
Had two garage sales selling almost everything
Chance took second job delivering pizzas 5 nights/week
Sold their home (used equity to become debt-free)
Put up old 'Charlie Brown' Christmas tree instead of buying fancy one

results.total_debt_paid: All consumer debt + full 6-month emergency fund
results.four_years_later: Debt-free including new house (36 years earlier than financial planner estimated)
non_financial_blessings: Chance was reunited with a 21-year-old son he had not seen since infancy

grand_prize_winners.key_lesson: What's bigger than the big check we received is the change in our lives. Once upon a time if we had won $50,000, we would have just spent it foolishly and then wondered where the money went.
grand_prize_winners.symbol: Still use the old Charlie Brown Christmas tree as a symbol of what they've accomplished and how they've changed their family tree.

forms_included.form: Major Components of a Healthy Financial Plan
forms_included.pledge: I (We) __________, (a) responsible adult(s), do hereby promise to take the above-stated actions by the above-stated dates to financially secure the well-being of my (our) family and myself (ourselves).

forms_included.description: Lists all assets (real estate, cars, cash, checking, savings, money market, mutual funds, retirement plan, stocks/bonds, cash value insurance, household items, jewelry, antiques, boat) minus liabilities (unsecured debt, credit card debt) to calculate total equity.

forms_included.instructions: Every dollar of your income should be allocated to some category on this sheet. Money 'left over' should be put back into a category. Almost every category (except debt) should have some dollar amount in it. This is a 'zero-based budget.'
notes: Fill in Subtotal for each subcategory and Total for each main category.
Fill in 'Actually Spent' column after the month.
Calculate '% of Take-Home Pay' for each category.
An * beside an item means use the 'envelope system.'
Emergency Fund should get ALL savings until 3-6 months of expenses saved.
Three copies of the form are provided for one quarter.

forms_included.note: These are only recommended percentages and will change dramatically if you have a very high or very low income.

forms_included.description: Implements the Monthly Cash-Flow Plan into real life. Four columns for up to four different pay periods per month. Each paycheck is fully allocated before received. Last entry should have '0' remaining, showing whole check is allocated.
instructions: As you allocate paycheck to an item, put remaining balance to the right of the slash.
Allocate ALL of your paycheck before you get paid.
Emergency Fund gets ALL savings until 3-6 months of expenses saved.

forms_included.for: Self-employed, commission, or royalty income earners
instructions: Ask: If I only have enough money to pay one thing, what would that be?
Move through the list in order of importance.
Saving should be a high priority.
The 'Cumulative Amount' column shows how far down the priority list a given check will reach.

forms_included.description: Tracks committed savings balances by category to prevent impulsive spending of savings.
COUNTDOWN TO FREEDOM!! Lists debts in order from smallest to largest payoff balance.
instructions: List debts smallest to largest by total payoff amount.
Redo this sheet each time you pay off a debt.
Keep old sheets to 'wallpaper the bathroom in your new debt-free house.'
New Payment = all payments on debts above + current minimum payment.
Cumulative Payments = running total of Payments Remaining.

forms_included.description: For when you cannot pay creditors what they request. Treat all creditors fairly and equally. Pay even the ones who haven't called.
forms_included.instructions: List all debts. Calculate each debt as a percentage of total debt. Pay that percentage of available income to each creditor.

seven_baby_steps.title: Save $1,000 Fast (Starter Emergency Fund)
seven_baby_steps.description: Build a $1,000 baby emergency fund before doing anything else. This prevents new debt when unexpected expenses arise while paying off debt.
seven_baby_steps.when_complete: When you have $1,000 in a savings account dedicated only to emergencies.

seven_baby_steps.title: The Debt Snowball
seven_baby_steps.description: List all debts (except the house) smallest to largest. Pay minimums on all except the smallest. Attack the smallest with every extra dollar. Roll payments to next debt when paid off.
seven_baby_steps.when_complete: When all debt except the home mortgage is paid off.

seven_baby_steps.title: Finish the Emergency Fund
seven_baby_steps.description: Save 3-6 months of expenses in a Money Market account. This is your fully funded emergency fund.
seven_baby_steps.when_complete: When you have 3-6 months of expenses saved.

seven_baby_steps.title: Invest 15% of Income in Retirement
seven_baby_steps.description: Invest 15% of before-tax gross income into Roth IRAs and pre-tax retirement plans (401k/403b). Order: 1) 401k to employer match, 2) Roth IRA to max, 3) Back to 401k to reach 15%.
seven_baby_steps.when_complete: When you are consistently investing 15% of gross income toward retirement.

seven_baby_steps.title: College Funding
seven_baby_steps.description: Save for children's college using ESAs (Education Savings Accounts) and/or 529 plans. Goal: $166.67/month per child from birth = enough for virtually any college.
seven_baby_steps.when_complete: When you have a college savings plan funded and on track for each child.

seven_baby_steps.title: Pay Off the Home Mortgage
seven_baby_steps.description: Pay off the home early. Put every extra dollar above living, retirement, and college toward the mortgage. Attack with gazelle intensity.
seven_baby_steps.when_complete: When the home mortgage is paid off. You are completely debt-free.

seven_baby_steps.title: Build Wealth and Give
seven_baby_steps.description: Build wealth intentionally. Use money for FUN, INVESTING, and GIVING. Reach the Pinnacle Point where your money makes more than you do (nest egg × 8% > annual expenses).
seven_baby_steps.when_complete: Never—this is a lifelong step. Keep building wealth and giving generously.

key_financial_principles: Personal finance is 80% behavior and 20% knowledge.
The borrower is slave to the lender (Proverbs 22:7).
Live like no one else so later you can live like no one else.
Gazelle intensity: total, sold-out, focused intensity to get out of debt.
The Debt Snowball: smallest to largest, not by interest rate—behavior modification over math.
Never borrow money for anything except possibly a 15-year fixed-rate mortgage.
Drive reliable used cars; never have a car payment.
Build an emergency fund before investing.
Invest 15% of gross income in retirement.
Save for college tax-free using ESAs and 529 plans.
Pay off the home mortgage early.
The three uses of money: FUN, INVESTING, and GIVING.
Always manage your own money—gather counsel but you make decisions.
Wealth amplifies character—be a good person first.
Giving is the most fun you will ever have with money.
